history.titleZh: Developer trains a small AI on a single RTX 3080 Ti gaming GPU to 'play' Pokémon Red
history.descriptionZh:
开发者 stmonty 在单张 RTX 3080 Ti 上训练了一个约 1250 万参数的小型 AI 世界模型，用于玩《宝可梦 红》。项目博文名为《Teaching a World Model to Play Pokémon》，目标是从大木博士实验室的存档出发，让模型自行选择初始宝可梦。该模型属于“世界模型”路线，受 Yann LeCun 共同参与的 LeWorldModel 研究启发；文章称 LeCun 去年离开 Meta，创立 AMI Labs，也采用类似方法构建世界模型。stmonty 在论坛表示，项目意在学习和娱乐，选择该模型是因为它能在消费级显卡上本地训练。模型于 9 月 20 日写成。

技术上，模型通过观察游戏画面来学习每个按键的作用。它并不预测完整的下一帧，而是把屏幕压缩为仅含 192 个数字的摘要表示，再在该压缩空间中学习动作后果。初始训练是“无奖励”的，模型不知道胜利条件，只学习环境动态；目标在后续规划阶段才引入。这一设计遵循 2026 年 3 月的一篇论文，该论文描述了一个约 1500 万参数的单一 JEPA 模型，可在单 GPU 上训练，与 stmonty 的规模相近。完整训练使用 42,382 张灰度帧、超过 1000 次短运行，数据来自大木博士实验室存档，包括脚本化路线、脚本路线混入随机按键以及随机游走。随机游走很关键：若只用干净运行数据，模型可能学会“对话框出现就按 A”，却永远学不会 B 键在该场景的作用。模型从头训练。

规划方面，模型以 14 次按键为一个计划长度，并只在模型内部尝试，而不是直接在游戏里试。每轮生成 512 个计划样本，搜索保留八分之一即 64 个，如此反复筛选，直到最终计划在游戏模拟器中执行。第一次尝试失败，玩家未能获得宝可梦；stmonty 推测原因是从模型自身预测继续做预测时，小误差会逐步累积。微调后的下一次尝试成功，模型选择了杰尼龟。随后从同一存档进行 100 多次运行，有 52 个计划成功获得初始宝可梦；作为对比，随机按键为 0 次成功，未训练模型仅 1 次成功。stmonty 也指出，从该存档反复按 A 本来就能推进，真正的目标是让模型自己发现解法。这一结果虽然有限，但证明小模型可以被定制用于特定任务。

下一步，开发者“可能仍会尝试”让模型从实验室开始，走到教授面前，完成对话，再实际选择宝可梦。但他怀疑难度会随计划长度指数增长，并认为“仅仅把当前模型变大”不太可能让模型通关。近期已有至少两个独立且成功的尝试用 Jev 决策模型配合 harness 或自定义代码通关《宝可梦 红》，这些方案更复杂；而小模型仍是爱好者现实可行的选项。项目代码已在 GitHub 以 lePokeRed 开源，推荐使用 CUDA GPU。总体来看，该案例展示了无奖励世界模型加规划在消费级硬件上的可行性，也暴露了长时程规划中误差累积的核心瓶颈；对游戏智能体、机器人等需要从视觉输入规划动作的应用有参考意义。

history.title: ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC
history.description: OpenAI says AI-assisted Jalapeño chip design "established a new baseline" for the industry, and there is already a lot of interest from others to learn how the company pulled it off.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter OpenAI’s Jalapeño ASIC is a seismic shift for the industry, not because of its efficiency or performance, but because of how it was designed. The company was clear from the jump that AI played a big role in the design process of Jalapeño, not only for the hardware itself, but also in the co-design with OpenAI’s software stack, allowing the ASIC to go from initial register-transfer level (RTL) to tapeout in a matter of just nine months. From concept to reveal, the timeline was less than two years. Richard Ho, head of hardware at OpenAI, says the timeline “established a new baseline,” and that the industry is already knocking on OpenAI’s door to learn how the company pulled it off.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible“The way I like to think about it is, we’ve established a new baseline. In the old baseline, you’re talking 18 months to two years, roughly. Often that’s even with some existing IP or some more legacy architecture design,” Ho told Tom’s Hardware Premium in an interview. “We’re starting from scratch here. We had nothing. There’s not a line of code here to refer to. What we’ve established is that there’s a new baseline that you can do with a very talented team with the help of AI. Now, does it get shorter? It depends on what you’re trying to do.”AI usage in chip design is nothing new, predating the era of LLMs entirely. The largest Electronic Design Automation (EDA) companies, Cadence and Synopsys, have a portfolio of AI-assisted chip design tools that have been around for several years. The models OpenAI used were its own internal models, however, and it leveraged both existing EDA tools and its new AI-assisted engineering workflow.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The engineering team used OpenAI’s agentic coding platform, Codex, for the Jalapeño design. “But we think that every engineering team in chip design should be able to use this as a new baseline, because it’s a proof point that the models that are in use — the AI models for us is mostly Codex, Sol, the one before Sol, and now we’re moving on to Astra. These are super capable. Even from when we started that work, back in November 2025, to when we taped out, the models improved enormously. Even from that moment to when we started doing the kernel optimization in May, when the chips were first coming online, we ourselves were shocked at how much better Codex was and what it could do,” Ho said. A free PCB viewer from Cadence Design. (Image credit: Cadence)Although AI was used during the entire development process, not only for design itself but also in writing and optimizing kernels, Ho continually reiterated the importance of talented engineers guiding those systems. The development story of Jalapeño is one of the few clear examples of AI bolstering a team of human workers, not displacing them. You may like Hot Chips 2026: OpenAI's Jalapeño AI ASIC unpacked OpenAI Jalapeño design interview transcript OpenAI's custom Jalapeno AI inference ASIC is for OpenAI’s internal use, but company leaves the door open to broader rollout Ho described the development cycle as a “good model” of how engineering teams should operate in the AI era. “This is how AI should be used. We didn’t replace our engineers; they just became super productive. With a smaller team of really good engineers with a lot of this AI stuff, you could do things faster and better than you could otherwise. I think that’s a good model of how engineering should be approached in the AI age.”Although OpenAI managed to get working silicon much faster than a traditional development cycle, it wasn’t free of issues. For starters, OpenAI’s B0 stepping of Jalapeño reportedly delivers up to a 25% improvement in performance per watt over the original A0 stepping. That’s closer to a generational improvement than stepping optimization, suggesting that, at least for a brand new hardware team, there may have been design oversights with the original stepping. Attributing that to AI or humans is anyone’s guess.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsOther frontier labs are circling for a slice of the pie, as well. Clive Chan, a key engineer on Jalapeño and the second-ever hardware hire at OpenAI, left the company in June to join the hardware team at Anthropic. Ho says there’s already been “a lot of interest in the industry” for OpenAI’s AI-assisted chip design process, and says that “we’ll see more about that quite shortly.”“I’m not going to preempt anything here. I can tell you that there’s a lot of interest in the industry, and I would also tell you that we feel that there is a lot of benefit in industry generally that we want to enable,” Ho said. “I think that’s something that we’ll see more about quite shortly, to be honest.”Ho referenced the dozens of AI-first chip design startups in Silicon Valley, suggesting OpenAI may eventually introduce tools of its own to aid other firms with AI chip development. “We have our take on that, and I think at some point we want to tell the world, “Here’s our take on it.” Fundamental to that is Codex and GPT-6 Astra coming out. Those are fundamental, and we can basically point to it; it’s not going to be slideware or vaporware. We can point to it and say, “Here’s what we did, here’s how we did it, and here’s what we got.” It’s going to be very concrete.” What to read next Silicon is starting to design silicon — how AI is being used in chipmaking, from EDA tools to OpenAI's Jalapeño and beyond OpenAI’s 700W Jalapeño ASIC outpaces 1,400W Nvidia flagship GPU Anthropic co-designing custom AI inference chips to bypass costly Nvidia GPUs (Image credit: OpenAI)What exactly the “it” Ho is referring to here remains a mystery, though given the context, it sounds like OpenAI may explore some way to productize its AI chip design workflow. Ho says Astra is a big step toward that, and we’ve already seen the model in action performing impressive feats, such as completing Portal autonomously.Although OpenAI leveraged its own models heavily for Jalapeño's design and validation, it didn’t completely break the mold of traditional EDA workflows, particularly at the end of the design process. Before tapeout, tools from companies like Synopsys and Cadence perform a series of tests for signoff, including static timing analysis and signal integrity analysis. Ho says that OpenAI used this typical EDA flow for Jalapeño.“But for sign-off, you need to use the standard EDA flows, and we did, because you want to make sure those results are good and correct. There’s no real alternative today. Part of it is this combination of standard flows optimized with AI, optimized by really good engineers,” Ho said.OpenAI shared a multi-generational roadmap for accelerators. It says its second-gen ASIC is approaching tape-out, and its third generation is already in development. Although Ho said that the Jalapeño development cycle establishes a new baseline for chip design timelines, he was cautious about calling that cycle and cadence.“Our projects and tape-outs will be dependent on the maturity level of the technologies. We can do very fast execution. Will we do those types of executions back-to-back? I doubt it, because the technology will not be ready for that, and I don’t want to tape out something that is 2% better than what I taped out before, because it’s not worth it to change a fleet,” Ho told us.The executive was also clear that the Jalapeño timeline isn’t necessarily the same timeline all chips will follow. There were some “pragmatic trade-offs” in the early architecture design, with the team avoiding emerging, complex design points like 3D stacking and co-packaged optics. “Will it take longer? Will it take nine months? I won't say it will take nine months… but I think it will go faster than if you didn't have AI models.” You can read the full transcript of the interview, which covers a wide range of topics, at Tom's Hardware Premium. history.titleZh: ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC
history.descriptionZh:
OpenAI 的 Jalapeño ASIC 被视为行业的一次地震式转变，原因不在于单纯的能效或性能，而在于它的设计方式。OpenAI 从一开始就明确，AI 在 Jalapeño 的设计过程中发挥了重要作用，不仅参与硬件本身，也参与了与 OpenAI 软件栈的协同设计，使这款 ASIC 从初始寄存器传输级（RTL）到流片仅用九个月，从概念到揭晓不到两年。OpenAI 硬件负责人 Richard Ho 表示，这一时间线“建立了一个新基线”，业界已经开始向 OpenAI 打听是如何做到的。传统芯片开发基线大约是 18 个月到两年，而且往往基于现有 IP 或较传统的架构设计；Jalapeño 则是从零开始，没有一行代码可供参考。Ho 称，这证明一支非常有才华的团队在 AI 帮助下可以做到过去难以想象的事情。

AI 用于芯片设计并非全新概念，早在 LLM 时代之前就已存在。Cadence 和 Synopsys 等大型 EDA 公司多年来一直提供 AI 辅助芯片设计工具。但 OpenAI 使用的是自家内部模型，并结合现有 EDA 工具与新的 AI 辅助工程流程。Jalapeño 的设计使用了 OpenAI 的代理式编码平台 Codex，模型组合包括 Codex、Sol、Sol 之前的模型，以及现在的 Astra。Ho 透露，从 2025 年 11 月开始这项工作，到流片时，模型能力已经大幅提升；到 2026 年 5 月芯片首次上线并进行内核优化时，Codex 的进步让团队自己都感到震惊。AI 不仅用于设计本身，也用于编写和优化内核。不过 Ho 反复强调，有才华的工程师指导这些系统仍然至关重要。Jalapeño 的开发故事是 AI 增强而非取代人类团队的少数清晰案例之一。他把这种开发周期描述为 AI 时代工程团队应有的“良好模式”：没有替换工程师，而是让他们变得超级高效；一支更小但更优秀的工程师团队，借助大量 AI 工具，可以更快、更好地完成工作。

在性能与设计迭代方面，OpenAI 的 Jalapeño B0 步进相比最初的 A0 步进，每瓦性能提升高达 25%。这更接近代际改进，而不是普通的步进优化，暗示对于一个全新的硬件团队来说，原始步进可能存在设计疏忽。至于应归因于 AI 还是人类，目前无法判断。相关报道还指出，700W 的 Jalapeño ASIC 性能超过了 1400W 的 Nvidia 旗舰 GPU。Jalapeño 是 OpenAI 内部使用的自定义 AI 推理 ASIC，但公司并未排除更广泛推广的可能。OpenAI 还公布了加速器的多代路线图：第二代 ASIC 已接近流片，第三代已在开发中。不过 Ho 对持续快速迭代持谨慎态度。他表示，项目与流片节奏取决于技术成熟度。OpenAI 可以快速执行，但不一定会背靠背地连续流片，因为技术可能尚未准备好，而且他不想只为了比上一代提升 2% 就流片，因为不值得为此更换整个机群。Jalapeño 的时间线也不一定适用于所有芯片。早期架构设计中有一些“务实的取舍”，团队避免了 3D 堆叠和共封装光学等新兴复杂设计点。会不会以后都只要九个月？Ho 不愿断言，但认为会比没有 AI 模型时更快。

设计流程上，OpenAI 虽然大量使用自家模型进行设计和验证，但并未完全打破传统 EDA 工作流，尤其在设计末期。流片前，Synopsys 和 Cadence 等公司的工具会执行一系列签核测试，包括静态时序分析和信号完整性分析。Ho 表示，OpenAI 在 Jalapeño 上使用了这种典型 EDA 流程。他说，签核必须使用标准 EDA 流程，因为要确保结果良好且正确，目前没有真正的替代方案。因此，Jalapeño 的成功来自标准流程、AI 优化和优秀工程师的组合。

这一事件的影响正在向行业扩散。Ho 称业界对 OpenAI 的 AI 辅助芯片设计流程“兴趣浓厚”，并暗示“很快会看到更多”。他表示不想提前透露，但强调行业普遍能从中受益，OpenAI 希望赋能更广泛的产业。他提到硅谷有数十家 AI 优先的芯片设计初创公司，暗示 OpenAI 可能最终推出自己的工具，帮助其他公司进行 AI 芯片开发。Codex 和 GPT-6 Astra 的推出是这一方向的基础。Ho 强调，这不会是幻灯片或空谈，而是可以具体展示“我们做了什么、怎么做的、得到了什么”。与此同时，其他前沿实验室也在争抢人才和机会。Jalapeño 的关键工程师、OpenAI 第二位硬件员工 Clive Chan 已于 6 月离开，加入 Anthropic 的硬件团队。Anthropic 也在联合设计自定义 AI 推理芯片，以绕开昂贵的 Nvidia GPU。OpenAI 的 Jalapeño 因此不仅是一款内部推理芯片，更可能成为 AI 辅助芯片设计新范式的起点，推动整个半导体行业重新思考工程团队的组织方式和芯片开发节奏。
